name: Gmail
summary: This guide describes how to set up OAuth 2.0 authorization for an application using the Gmail API, emphasizing the selection of appropriate API scopes, and provides important notes on sensitivity levels and the necessity of app verification for certain scopes.
decision: You must register your own application in Google Cloud, configure the OAuth consent screen, specify only the required Gmail API scopes, and if your app uses sensitive or restricted scopes, submit it for Google verification.

prerequisites.title: Google Cloud account
prerequisites.body: Access to the Google Cloud Console is required to register and configure your app.
prerequisites.note: App registration details require Google Cloud Console access.

steps.title: Register your app with Google Cloud
steps.body: Create a new project or select an existing project in Google Cloud Console and register your application to use Gmail API.
steps.note: Registration is implied as the first setup activity.

steps.title: Configure OAuth consent screen
steps.body: Set up your OAuth consent screen, entering app information and specifying the Gmail API scopes your app needs.
steps.note: Consent screen configuration is mentioned as part of the OAuth setup.

steps.title: Select and declare Gmail API scopes
steps.body: Choose the least permissive scopes necessary from the lists provided. Prefer non-sensitive scopes for easier verification.
steps.note: Lists of scope URIs are shown with recommendations on scope sensitivity.

steps.title: Submit for verification if necessary
steps.body: If you use sensitive or restricted scopes, or if your app is public, submit your app for verification through Google's process to avoid warnings and ensure users can authorize.
steps.note: Verification process necessity and its triggers are clearly outlined.
